messages:
Maya (PM): Quick sync 1: need to lock scope for the observability pilot for three customers. Candidate MVP: cost dashboard, error dashboard, a minimal tracing hook, per-route cost breakdown, simple error analytics, and basic alerting. Can we aim for ~6 sprints? Need concrete asks for the roadmap doc.

Ainsley (Eng): 6 sprints is tight but workable if we trim scope. MVP: dashboards + cost attribution + top error list = yes. Full-span ingestion and trace search should be v2. For MVP tracing we do trace-id propagation, span-count metrics, and sampled-span emission.

Raj (SRE): +1. Guardrails: default sampling 0.1 with per-route overrides. If we enable full spans w/o sampling we'll spike ingestion ~3x. Must have fail-open so user requests never block on trace backend.

Taylor (Data): Cost attribution: we can map tokens to route+model with current pipeline. Product decision: canonical route key (path vs api-key tag) and retention (30d vs 90d). 30d significantly cheaper.

Olivia (CS): Pilot customers (FinHealth, EduModel, ShopAlpha) want 90d for auditability. FinHealth requires PII redaction controls on any trace export.

Ainsley (Eng): Span-level PII redaction increases complexity. For MVP we'll provide a deny-list export and a manual redaction checklist; sanitizer ruleset (regex + header flags) is v2.

Maya (PM): Draft launch criteria: 1) Dashboards: cost by route/model, error rate timeseries, top-10 errors. 2) Tracing hook: trace-id propagation + span-count + sampled spans. 3) Cost: per-1k-token estimate visible on route view. 4) CS signoff from at least two pilots. OK?

Raj (SRE): Add platform SLO: ingestion path must not exceed 2x baseline CPU at pilot load. Fail-open spec: if trace backend down, requests proceed; emit negative metric and a log. Also alert: ingestion 99p latency >200ms for >5m -> page.

Ainsley (Eng): Buffer plan: 50MB per pod for spans; if exceeded drop non-critical spans and increment drop counters. Document buffer and backpressure behaviour. Prototype header: `X-Redwood-Trace: <trace-id>:<span-id>`. We'll provide a tiny SDK helper to inject.

Taylor (Data): Sampling config example we can ship quickly: `{"default_rate":0.1,"routes":{"/v1/generate":0.5}}`. We'll store this JSON blob per-tenant in config service.

Olivia (CS): I can get FinHealth to accept 30d for pilot if we provide strict PII redaction checklist + a roadmap commitment for 90d + sanitizer. I'll draft onboarding templates.

Maya (PM): Prioritization (must vs nice): MUST: dashboards (cost + errors), cost attribution, trace-id propagation, onboarding docs. NICE: span search, PII sanitizer, dynamic sampling UI.

Ainsley (Eng): High-level sprint plan: Sprint 1: spec, ingestion schema, trace header. Sprint 2: cost attribution pipeline + sampling config. Sprint 3: dashboards alpha (cost + top errors). Sprint 4: sampling controls + retention config. Sprint 5: CS docs + pilot onboarding. Sprint 6: polish + canary + mitigations.

Maya (PM): Action items: @Ainsley spec for minimal trace hook by EOD Fri; @Taylor infra delta estimate for 30d vs 90d by Wed; @Olivia confirm retention with FinHealth; @Raj define fail-open + buffer sizing. I'll add to roadmap tracker.

Raj (SRE): Will do. Also: require a non-blocking degrade mode and emit a metric `trace.ingest.dropped` when we drop spans.

Ainsley (Eng): Note: we'll gate full-span export behind an enterprise feature flag and explicit consent. For MVP, no external span exports.

deploy-bot: prod-deploy requested by @Ainsley for branch `obs/proto-trace` at 2026-03-23T14:12:00Z 1 canary started in product env.

Maya (PM): Good. No objections -> commit this scope and move span-search and PII sanitizer to backlog. :thumbsup:
